citation: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Employment Situation of Veterans — 2025 (news release USDL). Released April 28, 2026.
population: U.S. civilian noninstitutional population aged 18+, veterans and nonveterans, 2025 annual averages (CPS)
effect: Veteran unemployment 3.5% in 2025; nonveterans 4.2%; 17.3 million veterans
summary: BLS annual release on veteran labor-market status for calendar 2025. It gives unemployment rates for all veterans, Gulf War-era II veterans and nonveterans, and the veteran population count. The 2025 annual averages exclude October because the survey was not collected during the federal shutdown.
key_facts: 2025: unemployment rate for all veterans 3.5 percent (up from 3.0 percent in 2024).
2025: Gulf War-era II veterans 3.6 percent, little changed over the year.
2025: nonveterans 4.2 percent.
2025: 17.3 million veterans.
Caveat: 2025 annual figures exclude October because the survey was not collected during the federal shutdown; not strictly comparable with other years.
quotes: The jobless rate for all veterans increased over the year from 3.0 percent to 3.5 percent in 2025. (summary para.)
The unemployment rate for Gulf War-era II veterans was little changed over the year at 3.6 percent. (summary para.)
role_note: Carries the 2025 veteran and nonveteran unemployment rates and the veteran population count.

citation: U.S. Department of Defense. DoD SkillBridge — Program Overview; Industry/Employers. skillbridge.osd.mil, n.d. (industry page 'Updated: June 9, 2022').
publisher: U.S. Department of Defense (OUSD Personnel & Readiness)
population: Separating service members in their final 180 days of service; industry partners under a signed SkillBridge MOU
summary: DoD's official SkillBridge pages. They state the up-to-180-day permissive-duty window, that members keep military pay and benefits, that industry partners do not pay wages or benefits, and that participation requires a signed MOU. The industry page is at skillbridge.osd.mil/industry-employers.htm.
key_facts: Participation may last up to the final 180 days of service; members may be granted up to 180 days of permissive duty.
Members continue receiving military compensation and benefits during SkillBridge; participants are 'NOT eligible for wages or other benefits from industry partners.'
Employers may not take a member without a signed SkillBridge MOU; partners are expected to have defined training and a high probability of a job being available.
Overview page: approximately 200,000 members leave active duty each year; programs at over 140 installations (industry page, 2022).
Not stated on these pages: 10 U.S.C. 1143(e), DoDI 1322.29, or a 'no displacement of employees' clause.
quotes: Service members participating in DOD SkillBridge programs continue receiving their military compensation and benefits (program-overview.htm)
Service members can be granted up to 180 days of permissive duty (program-overview.htm)
NOT eligible for wages or other benefits from industry partners. (industry-employers.htm)
role_note: Carries the SkillBridge enabler's terms as DoD states them.

citation: U.S. Department of Labor, Veterans' Employment and Training Service. HIRE Vets Medallion Program. hirevets.gov, 2025.
population: Employers of any size applying for the HIRE Vets Medallion Award (small 1–50, medium 51–499, large 500+)
summary: DOL's official site for the award created by the HIRE Vets Act of 2017. It sets the criteria (veteran share of new hires, veteran retention, veteran share of employees), the integration-program requirements by tier, and application fees by employer size. The criteria text shown is the 2025 cycle.
key_facts: 2025 application window opened January 31, 2025; a 'Review 2026 Criteria' link exists but the criteria text shown is the 2025 cycle.
Small employers (1–50): Platinum requires 10% veteran new hires, 85% veteran retention, 10% veteran employees; Gold requires 7% / 75% / 7%.
The same percentage thresholds apply to medium and large employers; integration-program requirements rise with size.
Application fees: \$120 small, \$250 medium, \$640 large (same for Gold and Platinum).
quotes: Recognizing employers for their investments in recruiting, employing, and retaining our nation's heroes. (home page)
The Department of Labor will begin accepting applications for the 2025 HIRE Vets Medallion Award on January 31, 2025. (home page)
role_note: Carries the HIRE Vets Medallion criteria and fees.

citation: U.S. Department of Defense, Office of the Secretary. Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Program; final rule, 32 CFR part 170. 89 FR 83092, October 15, 2024 (effective December 16, 2024).
publisher: Federal Register / U.S. Department of Defense
population: Organizations Seeking Assessment (OSAs) that process, store or transmit FCI/CUI on DoD contracts; CMMC assessors and C3PAOs
summary: The program rule establishing CMMC levels, assessment types and the four-phase rollout. Level 1 is an annual self-assessment against the 15 FAR 52.204-21 requirements; Level 2 covers the 110 NIST SP 800-171 R2 requirements by self-assessment or C3PAO certification, every three years with annual affirmation. Current text sits at eCFR 32 CFR 170.3 (currency checked 2026-10-20).
key_facts: Published 2024-10-15 (89 FR 83092); effective 2024-12-16; codified at 32 CFR part 170.
Level 1 (Self): the OSA must meet all 15 FAR 52.204-21 requirements annually, no exceptions.
Level 2: 110 requirements derived from NIST SP 800-171 R2; Level 2 (C3PAO) requires hiring a C3PAO; a new assessment every three years; annual affirmation by the Affirming Official in SPRS (170.22).

Phase 1 begins on the effective date of the 48 CFR CMMC acquisition rule; Phase 2 one year after Phase 1; Phase 3 one year after Phase 2; Phase 4 (full implementation) one year after Phase 3 (32 CFR 170.3(e)).

Assessor personnel: a CMMC Certified Assessor (CCA) candidate must first be a CMMC Certified Professional (CCP) and complete a Tier 3 background investigation or equivalent; CCAs make final Level 2 (C3PAO) determinations.
POA&Ms must be closed within 180 days of the Conditional CMMC Status Date (170.21).
quotes: The OSA must comply with the 15 security requirements set by FAR clause 52.204-21. (Level 1 discussion)
OSAs must hire a C3PAO to conduct an assessment of the OSA's compliance with the 110 security requirements (Level 2 (C3PAO) discussion)
In order to be a CCA, a candidate must first be a CCP (assessor requirements)
Begins one calendar year following the start date of Phase 1. (32 CFR 170.3(e)(2), eCFR)
role_note: Carries CMMC level content, phase structure and assessor-personnel requirements.

citation: U.S. Department of Defense, Defense Acquisition Regulations System. Assessing Contractor Implementation of Cybersecurity Requirements (DFARS Case 2019-D041); final rule, 48 CFR parts 204, 212, 217, 252. 90 FR 43560, September 10, 2025 (effective November 10, 2025).
publisher: Federal Register (govinfo) / U.S. Department of Defense
population: Offerors and contractors on DoD solicitations and contracts that will process, store or transmit FCI or CUI; subcontractors by flow-down
effect: 1,104 small entities affected in year one; 229,818 by year four and beyond
summary: The acquisition rule that puts CMMC into DFARS (provision 252.204-7025; clause 252.204-7021; subpart 204.75). It makes CMMC status a condition of award, phases application in over three years with full application beginning three years and one day after the effective date, and requires an affirming official. It gives entity-count and burden estimates, including small entities.
key_facts: The CMMC requirement must be met at time of award; contracting officers shall not award without the required CMMC status in SPRS.

Phase-in: the requirement is applied selectively 'until three years after the effective date of the rule'; full application 'Beginning three years and one day after the effective date of the rule'; by the fourth year all offerors on applicable solicitations.

Burden estimates: 1,104 small entities affected in year one; 229,818 small entities by year four and beyond; 337,968 unique entities in total; about 5 minutes to post a self-assessment result in SPRS.
Contractors need an affirming official (32 CFR 170.4) to complete an affirmation of continuous compliance.
quotes: the estimated number of small entities to which the rule will apply is 1,104 in year one (Regulatory Flexibility Act analysis)
By year four, and beyond, the estimated number of impacted small entities will be 229,818 (Regulatory Flexibility Act analysis)
Beginning three years and one day after the effective date of the rule (phase-in discussion)
role_note: Carries the DFARS CMMC effective date, award condition, phase-in wording and small-entity counts.

citation: Federal Acquisition Regulation 52.222-54, Employment Eligibility Verification (Jan 2025), and FAR 22.1803 (clause prescription). acquisition.gov, FAC 2026-01, effective March 13, 2026.
population: Federal contractors on solicitations and contracts exceeding \$150,000 with performance of 120 days or more in the United States; subcontractors with subcontracts over \$3,500
summary: The FAR E-Verify clause and its prescription. FAR 22.1803 inserts the clause in contracts that exceed \$150,000, except work performed only outside the U.S., performance under 120 days, and COTS-type items. The clause sets 30-day enrollment, 90-day start-of-use and 3-business-day new-hire verification windows and defines 'employee assigned to the contract'. Prescription page: acquisition.gov/far/22.1803.
key_facts: FAR 22.1803 (FAC 2026-01, effective 2026-03-13): clause inserted in 'all solicitations and contracts that exceed \$150,000', except (a) work only outside the U.S., (b) period of performance less than 120 days, (c) COTS items and near-COTS/bulk-cargo variants and associated commercial services.

A contractor not enrolled at award must enroll as a Federal Contractor in E-Verify within 30 calendar days of award; within 90 calendar days of enrollment it begins using E-Verify for new hires within 3 business days after date of hire.
Employees assigned to the contract: verification initiated within 90 calendar days after enrollment or within 30 calendar days of assignment, whichever is later.
'Employee assigned to the contract' excludes employees who normally perform support work such as indirect or overhead functions without substantial duties on the contract.
Flow-down: subcontracts over \$3,500 that include work performed in the United States.
The threshold on the page reads '\$150,000'; it is not expressed as 'the simplified acquisition threshold' there.
quotes: Enroll as a Federal Contractor in the E-Verify program within 30 calendar days of contract award; (52.222-54(b)(1)(i))
Insert the clause at 52.222-54, Employment Eligibility Verification, in all solicitations and contracts that exceed $150,000 (FAR 22.1803)
Are for a period of performance of less than 120 days; or (FAR 22.1803(b))
role_note: Carries the E-Verify gate's threshold, exceptions and timing windows.

citation: Executive Order 14173, Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity (signed 2025-01-21; 90 FR 8633, 2025-01-31); and U.S. Department of Labor, OFCCP, Rescission of Executive Order 11246 Implementing Regulations, final rule, 91 FR 54444, 2026-08-21 (effective 2026-10-26).
publisher: Federal Register / U.S. Department of Labor, OFCCP
population: Federal contractors and subcontractors; 41 CFR chapter 60
summary: EO 14173 revoked EO 11246 on 2025-01-21 with a 90-day period in which contractors could continue to comply with the scheme in effect on January 20, 2025 (OFCCP's page gives 2025-04-21 as the wind-down date), and directed OFCCP to cease holding contractors responsible for affirmative action under that order. The 2026 final rule removes the EO 11246 regulations (41 CFR parts 60-1, 60-2, 60-3, 60-4, 60-20, 60-40, 60-50, 60-999) and strips EO 11246 components from part 60-30, effective 2026-10-26. EO text: federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/31/2025-02097.
key_facts: Sec. 3(b)(i): EO 11246 of September 24, 1965 revoked, signed 2025-01-21.
Sec. 3(b)(i): for 90 days from the order date, contractors may continue to comply with the regulatory scheme in effect on January 20, 2025 (OFCCP page: 2025-04-21).
Sec. 3(b)(ii): OFCCP directed to immediately cease promoting diversity and holding contractors responsible for affirmative action under EO 11246.
Rule published 2026-08-21 at 91 FR 54444; effective 2026-10-26; docket OFCCP-2025-0001.
Rescinds 41 CFR parts 60-1, 60-2, 60-3, 60-4, 60-20, 60-40, 60-50 and 60-999; amends 60-30 to remove EO 11246 procedures.
quotes: Executive Order 11246 of September 24, 1965 (Equal Employment Opportunity), is hereby revoked. (Sec. 3(b)(i))
Federal contractors may continue to comply with the regulatory scheme in effect on January 20, 2025. (Sec. 3(b)(i))
This rule is effective on October 26, 2026. (DATES)
Accordingly, the U.S. Department of Labor publishes this final rule to rescind the implementing regulations (SUMMARY)
role_note: Carries the EO 11246 revocation and the 2026 rescission of its regulations.

citation: U.S. Department of Labor, OFCCP. Modifications to the Regulations Implementing the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, as Amended; final rule (RIN 1250-AA19). 91 FR 54234, August 21, 2026 (effective September 21, 2026); correction 2026-17757, August 31, 2026.
publisher: Federal Register / U.S. Department of Labor, OFCCP
population: Federal contractors with a contract of \$200,000 or more (VEVRAA coverage, inflation-adjusted); AAP required at 50+ employees and a \$200,000+ contract
summary: Amends 41 CFR part 60-300 to remove EO 11246 cross-references, move administrative-enforcement procedures into the VEVRAA regulations (60-300.65), and reflect the inflation-adjusted \$200,000 coverage threshold. VEVRAA affirmative-action and nondiscrimination obligations continue. A correction notice was published 2026-08-31 (FR Doc. 2026-17757; not read).
key_facts: Published 2026-08-21 (91 FR 54234); effective 2026-09-21; docket OFCCP-2025-0002.
Revised 41 CFR 60-300.40(a): an AAP is required of every Government contractor with 50 or more employees and a contract of \$200,000 or more.
Rule text: the VEVRAA coverage threshold increased from \$150,000 to \$200,000 (inflation adjustment).
A law-firm alert (secondary, not relied on) describes veteran self-identification invitations, hiring benchmarks and VETS-4212 reporting as retained; not confirmed in the rule text read.
quotes: This rule is effective September 21, 2026. (DATES)
every Government contractor that has 50 or more employees and a contract of $200,000 or more (41 CFR 60-300.40(a) as revised)
affirmative action to employ and advance in employment qualified covered veterans (Background)
role_note: Carries the VEVRAA AAP threshold and the 2026 rule's effective date.

citation: U.S. Department of Labor, OFCCP. Modifications to the Regulations Implementing Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as Amended; final rule (RIN 1250-AA18). 91 FR 54482, August 21, 2026 (effective September 21, 2026; part 60-30 amendment effective December 21, 2026).
publisher: Federal Register / U.S. Department of Labor, OFCCP
population: Federal contractors covered by Section 503 (41 CFR part 60-741); AAP at 50+ employees and a \$50,000+ contract
summary: Amends 41 CFR part 60-741: rescinds the disability self-identification requirement (60-741.42) and the 7% utilization goal and utilization analysis (60-741.45), removes EO 11246 cross-references, and folds administrative procedures into the Section 503 rules. Nondiscrimination provisions and the written AAP requirement remain.
key_facts: Published 2026-08-21 (91 FR 54482); effective 2026-09-21 except the 41 CFR part 60-30 amendment, effective 2026-12-21; docket OFCCP-2025-0003.
Rescinds 41 CFR 60-741.42 (invitation to self-identify disability status) and the utilization goal and analysis in 60-741.45.
Retains nondiscrimination provisions and the AAP for contractors with 50 or more employees and a Federal contract or subcontract of \$50,000 or more (60-741.40(b)).

OFCCP page (undated, accessed 2026-10-22): 'Section 503 and VEVRAA, along with their implementing regulations, remain in effect'; the Section 503/VEVRAA AAP certification period 'will remain closed'; pending compliance reviews administratively closed; VAHBP moratorium through 2027-05-07.
quotes: This rule is effective September 21, 2026, except for amendatory instruction 1 (DATES)
The regulations' nondiscrimination provisions remain intact. (Executive Summary)
Section 503 and VEVRAA, along with their implementing regulations, remain in effect. (dol.gov/agencies/ofccp)
role_note: Carries the Section 503 AAP threshold, the rescinded self-ID and 7% goal, and OFCCP's status statements.

citation: 10 U.S.C. § 4093, Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Defense Education Program. U.S. Code (Office of the Law Revision Counsel), text current through August 4, 2026.
publisher: U.S. House Office of the Law Revision Counsel
population: U.S. citizens (plus up to five non-citizens per year under subsection (g)) pursuing associate, undergraduate or advanced degrees in critical skills or disciplines
summary: The statute authorizing the SMART scholarship-for-service program. The service obligation is employment with the Department of Defense, including active duty; the statute contains no provision for contractor employment to satisfy it. The program's own site is JavaScript-rendered and could not be read.
key_facts: A recipient must agree to accept and continue employment 'with the Department' for the period of obligated service (text current through 2026-08-04).
The statute contains no provision for contractor employment to satisfy the obligation; the phrase 'at a facility of the Department' does not appear.
Eligibility: U.S. citizen pursuing a degree in a critical skill or discipline at an accredited institution; non-citizen awards capped at five per year (subsec. (g)).
quotes: enter into a written agreement to accept and continue employment for the period of obligated service (10 U.S.C. 4093)
with the Department, including by serving on active duty in the Armed Forces (10 U.S.C. 4093)
role_note: Carries the SMART service obligation as the statute states it.
